archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (shot volume)
archetype.definition: A Detroit team that is out-shooting and slightly out-chancing opponents for the first time in years, with a .500-ish record held down by finishing and a leaky penalty kill rather than by how it plays at 5-on-5.

report.headline: Detroit is driving play like never before; the pucks just haven't gone in
report.take:
Eight games in, the Red Wings sit seventh in the Atlantic at 3-3-2 and 22nd on the site. Their pace of 82 standings points would land them right back where they have lived for five years, outside the playoffs. The underlying numbers describe a different team. Detroit is putting 30.5 shots a game on goal, fifth in the league and well above the 27.2 average. Its 5-on-5 share of expected goals is 51.8% and its shot-attempt share is 52%. In none of the last five seasons did this franchise clear 49% on either. Last year's xGF % was 48.8% and the year before 47.8%.

What is holding the record down is finishing. The skaters are converting 7.8% of their shots, 29th in the league against an 11.3% average. That leaves an all-situations PDO of 97.6, and it is why a team generating that much volume ranks 28th in offense at 2.5 goals a game. Some of that is roster: the forward group grades C-, Lucas Raymond has no goals on 23 shots, and Andrew Copp is getting 19.5 minutes a night with a 38.2% xGF. Most of it, though, is the kind of cold spell that eight games produce. The scoring is coming from Alex DeBrincat (five goals, fifth among right wingers) and rookie-tab standout Michael Brandsegg-Nygård (8th among right wingers, 65% xGF in sheltered minutes). Beyond those two it has been thin.

The real worries are at the other end. The penalty kill is at 69%, 28th and ten points under the league, and that is a problem a strong 5-on-5 game can't fully cover. The crease is split in an odd way. Team GSAx is +4, eighth in the league, but all of that belongs to Daniil Tarasov (.965, +5.4 in two starts). John Gibson has taken six of the eight starts at .873 and -1.5, which is why the goaltending grades D+. Close-game luck has been roughly neutral at +0.5, unlike last season's +5.4 cushion, so this record isn't flattering the team. If anything it undersells it.

The direction is up. Shooting percentage this far below the league tends to climb back toward the mean. A team taking this many shots will start scoring three-plus a night when it does. If the kill gets merely average and Gibson finds his level, or Tarasov takes more of the net, Detroit has the profile of a playoff-bubble team, and its shot share is better than any Wings team in this history.

strengths.title: Shot volume and 5-on-5 control
strengths.body: Detroit is fifth in shots on goal a game and above water in both expected-goal and shot-attempt share. That is a real change from five straight seasons under 49% xGF. It is the most sustainable thing on the sheet, because shot share stabilizes much faster than shooting percentage. Over eight games it still needs confirming, but it is the foundation of any optimism here.

strengths.title: DeBrincat and the kid on the right
strengths.body: Alex DeBrincat (9 points, +8, 57.5% xGF) and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård (6 points, +8, 65% xGF) rank fifth and eighth among right wingers. They are the reason the offense isn't worse. Brandsegg-Nygård is doing it in 15.3 minutes, so a bigger role is an obvious lever.

strengths.title: Seider anchoring the back end
strengths.body: Moritz Seider is logging 25.7 minutes with a 59.2% xGF and ranks 16th among 242 defensemen, helping the blueline to a C+ grade. With Justin Faulk chipping in offense, the defense is the steadiest group on the roster.

concerns.title: Penalty kill bleeding goals
concerns.body: A 69% kill ranks 28th and sits ten points under the league average. This team has been here before: it posted 70.1% in 2024-25 and missed the playoffs. It is the one weakness that out-shooting opponents at 5-on-5 can't offset. Some rebound is likely, but it is the biggest drag on the standings right now.

concerns.title: Gibson's starts vs Tarasov's results
concerns.body: Gibson has made six of eight starts with an .873 save % and negative GSAx, while Tarasov has stopped .965 and ranks fifth among 65 goalies. The team's +4 GSAx is entirely Tarasov. Two starts is far too few to crown him, but the current split of work is costing Detroit, and it shows in the D+ grade.

concerns.title: Finishing and forward depth
concerns.body: The skaters are shooting 7.8%, 29th in the league. Raymond is scoreless on 23 shots, and Copp and Kolesar are underwater in heavy and depth minutes. Most of the shooting slump should regress upward, but the C- forward grade says part of it is a thin middle six, and the power play at 17.9% is below the league too.

trend.note: An 0-2 start gave way to a run of losses that included two overtime points, then two straight wins to close the stretch. The last five games produced a .600 points percentage, better than the season mark, even though the goal differential didn't improve.

weekAhead.headline: Four-game western swing, three against leaky defenses
weekAhead.body:
Detroit spends the week on the road: Seattle, Vancouver, Calgary, then Edmonton. Road travel aside, this is about as good a set of opponents as a shooting-starved team could ask for. Vancouver is 32nd on the site with the league's worst penalty kill and a .865 save %. Calgary's goalies rank dead last in both save % and GSAx. Both teams also give up more than 29 shots a night, so Detroit's volume should finally meet goaltending that lets some through.

Seattle beat Detroit 6-3 in Detroit already. Its record rests on a 105.3 PDO and top-five shooting, while it owns only 44.5% of expected goals and allows 31.7 shots a game, 30th. That is a regression candidate Detroit should out-shoot. Edmonton is the real test: first in offense and 6-1-1, but riding a league-best 108.1 all-situations PDO with below-average goaltending and a 70.8% kill. Taking five or six points from the trip is a reasonable bar.

keyMatchups.title: Volume shooters meet Calgary's goaltending
keyMatchups.body: Calgary's goalies sit last in save % and GSAx, and its defense allows centers more points over expectation than almost anyone. Detroit's centers need it: Copp, Rasmussen and Larkin have two or three points apiece. This is the likeliest night for the shooting slump to break.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit's power play vs Vancouver's kill
keyMatchups.body: Vancouver kills just 58.1% of penalties, last in the league, and allows wingers and defensemen well above expectation. Raymond and Arvidsson carry three PP points each. A struggling 17.9% power play gets its softest opponent of the young season.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit's kill vs Edmonton's firepower
keyMatchups.body: Edmonton leads the league in shooting and converts 25% of its power plays, while Detroit kills 69%. Detroit should own the 5-on-5 game against a 48% CF team. Whether it wins the night depends on staying out of the box.

weekAhead.watch: How the four starts split between Gibson and Tarasov. A back-loaded road week is the natural time to find out whether Tarasov's start is real.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 82 points undersells this team. A skater group shooting 7.8% on top-five shot volume won't stay there. Even a partial climb toward the league's 11.3% turns a 28th-ranked offense into a middle-of-the-pack one. The 5-on-5 shares are the best of any recent Detroit team, and the close-game luck that propped up last season's 92 points is absent so far. That means the base is more honest. Expect the goal differential to drift toward even and the record to follow.

The ceiling is capped by the things that are less likely to fix themselves. A penalty kill that has sat near 70% before, a forward group that grades C- beyond its top two right wingers, and a goaltending picture where the starter is underperforming the backup. Realistically this is a bubble team, somewhere in the high 80s to mid 90s in points. Breaking the playoff drought depends mostly on the kill and the crease.
swingFactors: Gibson's save % or a shift of starts to Tarasov
Penalty kill climbing toward league average
Raymond and the centers converting their shots

confidence.note: Eight games: shot share is suggestive, shooting and save % are mostly noise.
